title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #12

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How many legs does a spider have? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Ten
   C. Six
   D. Four

2. Which part takes back most of the water from the leftover food? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach
   B. Gullet
   C. Mouth
   D. Large intestine

3. Which of these parts is found after the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Gullet
   C. Mouth
   D. Tongue

4. Which of these is non-decomposable? (1 mark)
   A. Plastic bottle
   B. Fruit peel
   C. Dung
   D. Dry leaves

5. Which of these can cause stomach ache? (1 mark)
   A. Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
   B. Drinking clean water
   C. Washing hands
   D. Brushing teeth

6. Which of these is non-decomposable waste? (1 mark)
   A. Banana peel
   B. Egg shells
   C. Leaves
   D. Tin can

7. A flash of light in the sky during a storm is a natural source of light. What is it? (1 mark)
   A. A car headlight
   B. A solar lamp
   C. A lantern
   D. Lightning

8. What does a translucent roof sheet do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes light
   B. Lets some light in
   C. Creates sound
   D. Blocks all light

9. What is an invertebrate? (1 mark)
   A. An animal with hair
   B. An animal that flies
   C. An animal with a backbone
   D. An animal without a backbone

10. Where does the digestive tube begin? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Stomach
   C. Mouth
   D. Anus

11. Which of these do we measure using litres? (1 mark)
   A. Mass of a book
   B. Volume of juice
   C. Time of a race
   D. Length of a rope

12. Why should candles and paraffin lamps be kept away from curtains? (1 mark)
   A. They make curtains bright
   B. They can start a fire
   C. They make curtains dry
   D. They make curtains cold

13. A sweet potato vine cutting grows roots and becomes a new plant. Which sign of life is shown? (1 mark)
   A. Breathing out
   B. Dying
   C. Removing waste
   D. Reproducing

14. Which of these is a way that people benefit from plants? (1 mark)
   A. They cause floods
   B. They make noise
   C. They give plastic
   D. They give food, shade and wood

15. In a school, who could check that bins are emptied and clean? (1 mark)
   A. Class monitors
   B. Only the wind
   C. Nobody
   D. Only the visitors

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. State two ways of reducing friction. (2 marks)

17. Describe the natural and artificial sources of light and explain the difference. (5 marks)

18. Describe how a bean seed grows into a young plant. (3 marks)

19. Give three uses of friction in daily life. (3 marks)

20. Name the three Rs of waste management. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — Eight
   Spiders have eight legs.

2. D — Large intestine
   The large intestine takes back water.

3. A — Small intestine
   Food moves from the stomach to the small intestine.

4. A — Plastic bottle
   Plastic does not rot easily.

5. A — Eating too fast or germs in dirty food
   Fast eating and dirty food can cause stomach pain.

6. D — Tin can
   Metal does not rot easily.

7. D — Lightning
   Lightning is a natural flash of light.

8. B — Lets some light in
   It lets daylight in but you cannot see through it clearly.

9. D — An animal without a backbone
   Invertebrates have no backbone.

10. C — Mouth
   Food enters the body through the mouth.

11. B — Volume of juice
   Litres measure volume.

12. B — They can start a fire
   Flames can set cloth on fire.

13. D — Reproducing
   Making a new plant from part of an old plant is reproduction.

14. D — They give food, shade and wood
   Plants give us food, shade, medicine, wood and clean air.

15. A — Class monitors
   Monitors can share the responsibility.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smoothen surfaces, use oil or grease, use rollers, use ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Natural sources are found in nature such as the sun, stars, lightning and fireflies. Artificial sources are made by people such as bulbs, torches and candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for natural and artificial, 1 mark for examples of each and 1 mark for the difference.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: The seed takes in water and a root comes out first and goes down. Then a shoot grows up and opens into leaves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for water and seed, 1 mark for root first, 1 mark for shoot and leaves.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Brakes, shoes gripping the ground, lighting matches, rough tyres, sharpening tools.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: Reduce, reuse and recycle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.
